web_evidence.title: Excerpt from The Lost Apothecary by Sarah Penner
web_evidence.note: A permission-authorized, sustained Chapter 1 excerpt headed “Nella” consistently narrates Nella’s actions, perceptions, history, and secrets as “I,” “me,” and “my.” Its scope is limited to the opening narrator.

web_evidence.title: Sarah Penner Writing Styles in The Lost Apothecary
web_evidence.note: The point-of-view analysis explicitly identifies Nella, Eliza, and Caroline as the novel’s three first-person narrators and gives first-person openings from all three strands.

web_evidence.title: The Indelible Mark of Women in “The Lost Apothecary”
web_evidence.note: In an author interview, the dual-timeframe structure is described as following three women; Penner confirms that Eliza narrates alongside Nella and that Eliza’s scenes were deliberately told from Eliza’s point of view. This corroborates the sustained multi-narrator structure, while the grammatical person is established by the excerpt and explicit POV source.

Checked the author’s official book page and library/retail results; they confirmed three women and two timelines but did not explicitly establish grammatical narrative person, so they were not used as person-supporting evidence.
person_note: The book’s controlling narration consists of alternating chapters by Nella, Eliza, and Caroline, but all three narrate as participating first-person speakers; multiple first-person narrators therefore yield FIRST, not ALTERNATING. Numerous event quotes independently expose “I,” “me,” “my,” or participant-inclusive “we,” including narratorial beats embedded in two dialogue-heavy quotations. Universal “you” statements and standalone maxims are local gnomic material, not second-person base narration. The authorized opening establishes Nella’s sustained first-person voice, and the whole-book POV analysis explicitly resolves the other two strands as first person; no credible contrary person evidence was found.
